comment: Work queue for the AXIOM swarm. The reviewer (human or Claude) edits this file to steer the search.

problems.statement: forall n >= 2: exists x >= 1: exists y >= 1: exists z >= 1: 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z
problems.notes: open; blind 0.3 run reduced it to primes in 36 classes mod 2520

problems.statement: forall n >= 2: exists x >= 1: exists y >= 1: exists z >= 1: 5/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z
problems.notes: open; blind 0.3 run reduced it to primes in 12 classes mod 2520

problems.statement: abc conjecture (Masser-Oesterle): for every eps > 0 there is K(eps) such that for all coprime positive integers a + b = c, c <= K(eps) * rad(a*b*c)^(1+eps). This queue entry runs the triple hunter, not a proof.
problems.notes: search-only: coprime a+b=c maximizing q=log(c)/log(rad(abc)); merge re-verifies every triple exactly

problems.statement: All coprime positive a + b = c with rad(a*b*c) | 2*3*5 (the S-unit equation for S={2,3,5}). This is a finite completeness certificate; it says nothing about the abc conjecture.
problems.notes: VALIDATED against the published 17-triple list; merge runs the independent checker; abc conjecture remains OPEN

problems.statement: Szpiro's conjecture on elliptic curves implies the abc conjecture. No proof is claimed here.
problems.notes: unproved idea; any candidate argument must be Lean against lean/Abc/Statement.lean, no sorry, no new axioms

problems.statement: The polynomial abc theorem of Mason and Stothers. It is proved and available in Mathlib but does not imply the integer abc conjecture.
problems.notes: polynomial analogue only; Mathlib Polynomial.abc; not a route to the integer statement

problems.statement: Effective upper bounds for c in terms of rad(abc) from linear forms in logarithms. These are partial bounds, not abc.
problems.notes: partial result; far weaker than abc; see swarm/abc_routes.md for citations

problems.statement: Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmuller theory claims a proof of abc. The claim is disputed and is not accepted as a proof here.
problems.notes: disputed; described neutrally; no IUT claim is used by this repository
